q: Why is a P99 estimate noisier than a P50 from the same runs?
o: only about 1% of runs fall beyond the P99
the P99 uses a different seed
why: The far tail is informed by very few runs.

q: A running-mean plot shows sudden late jumps. The most likely cause is …
o: a heavy tail: rare huge outcomes
why: Rare extreme values dominate the mean when they arrive.

q: A running estimate that has settled shows the answer is right.
why: Myth. It shows the computation converged; a biased model settles on the wrong value.

q: How can you put an interval on a simulated P80?
o: order statistics or the spread across batches
why: The count of runs below the true quantile is binomial, and batch spread works for any statistic.
